itens.titulo: Marvell to buy Lumentum in $115 billion deal in AI data-center bet
itens.descricao: Marvell to buy Lumentum in $115 billion deal in AI data-center bet CNBC
trechos: Marvell Technology is buying optical-components maker Lumentum in a deal valued at $115 billion, as the custom chipmaker steps up its challenge to larger rival Broadcom amid an AI spending boom.
The deal, announced on Monday, is one of the biggest in 2026 and among the boldest corporate bets yet on an AI boom that chip executives expect to underpin industry demand for years.
AI chip giant Nvidia invested $2 billion each in Marvell and Lumentum earlier this year.
But its market value has since surged to more than $170 billion, thanks to its role in helping tech giants such as Amazon develop custom AI chips and networking technology for data centers.

Marvell notched one of its biggest wins in August, signing a deal to supply chips that sit alongside Google's AI processors worth up to $120 billion in sales through fiscal 2033, giving the search giant the right to buy a $12.2 billion stake.

Lumentum could benefit from proposed Chinese ban Since the Marvell-Lumentum talks were first reported late last month, Lumentum's shares have fallen about 8% and Marvell about 22%, as a broad-based chip selloff accelerated following Intel's weak forecast.
It closed a $3.5 billion purchase of Celestial AI in February as rising use of AI agents and chatbots drives demand for faster optical links connecting thousands of chips in AI data centers.

Shares of Marvell hit a record high in June after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang called the custom chipmaker the next "trillion-dollar company." Its annual revenue has more than doubling from $3 billion in fiscal 2021 to $8.2 billion in fiscal 2026.

itens.titulo: Marvell Strikes $115B Deal To Acquire Lumentum: CEO Sees ‘Once In A Generation’ Opportunity In AI Optical Shift
itens.descricao: Marvell Strikes $115B Deal To Acquire Lumentum: CEO Sees ‘Once In A Generation’ Opportunity In AI Optical Shift Yahoo Finance
trechos: - The companies expect more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost synergies.
- Lumentum also reported $1.26 billion in first-quarter revenue, beating estimates.
Marvell (MRVL) on Monday announced a $115 billion all-stock deal to acquire Lumentum (LITE), with Marvell CEO Matt Murphy calling it a "once in a generation" deal.
"AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation," said Murphy.

"The companies that move first and help define this transition will set the standard for decades to come" MRVL stock was up around 1% in pre-market trade, paring earlier gains, while LITE stock gained as much as 2.5%.
Under the new deal, Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.500 shares of Marvell for each Lumentum share they own.
The companies said the exchange ratio implies a price of about $1,132 per Lumentum share, a premium of about 23.9%.
After the deal closes, Marvell shareholders will own about 67% of the combined company and Lumentum shareholders about 33%, on a fully diluted basis.

itens.descricao: Lumentum: Fiscal Q1 Earnings Snapshot Yahoo Finance
trechos: (AP) — Lumentum Holdings Inc. (LITE) on Monday reported fiscal first-quarter earnings of $360.3 million.
On a per-share basis, the San Jose, California-based company said it had net income of $3.54.
Earnings, adjusted for one-time gains and costs, were $4.57 per share.
The average estimate of seven analysts surveyed by Zacks Investment Research was for earnings of $4.22 per share.
The optical networking products maker posted revenue of $1.26 billion in the period, also exceeding Street forecasts.
Seven analysts surveyed by Zacks expected $1.25 billion.
For the current quarter ending in December, Lumentum expects its per-share earnings to range from $5.90 to $6.20.
The company said it expects revenue in the range of $1.58 billion to $1.63 billion for the fiscal second quarter.
